title: Resume vCenter role pagination after access-token expiry
prompt:
Platform engineering needs a deterministic inventory of vCenter authorization roles, but its authenticated SDK handle's access token can expire on a continuation page. Finish the `VcfVcenterRoleInventory` PowerShell module so it refreshes the caller-owned SDK connection, retries the exact failed page, and returns the complete inventory without discarding roles already collected.

Read the protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. The focused contract was projected directly from `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the immutable VCF 9.1 commit recorded in both files. The YAML specification, not a rendered documentation page, is the wire authority. The only vSphere Automation operationId in scope is exactly `Vcenter.Authorization.Roles_list`.

VCF PowerCLI 9.1 is installed by the environment. The supplied manifest must continue to require `VMware.Sdk.vSphere` version `13.5.0.25380678`. Do not install, copy, generate, vendor, intercept, or replace any VMware module, SDK assembly, binding, or OpenAPI file. In the production path, lazily use `Initialize-VcenterAuthorizationRolesIterationSpec` and `Invoke-VcenterAuthorizationRolesList`; do not bypass the SDK with `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, `HttpClient`, curl, raw sockets, or a subprocess.

Preserve the supplied signatures and export exactly these two functions:

- `New-VcfVcenterRoleInventorySession -Server <object> -RefreshConnection <scriptblock> [-OperationInvoker <scriptblock>]` returns an independent session and performs no network request. `Server` is an already authenticated vSphere SDK server handle. `RefreshConnection` receives the expired handle and must return a newly authenticated handle. `OperationInvoker` is the protected verifier seam; when omitted, dispatch through the two generated VCF PowerCLI cmdlets named above.
- `Get-VcfVcenterRoleInventory -Session <object> [-PageSize <int64>]` retrieves every page through `Vcenter.Authorization.Roles_list`. `PageSize` defaults to the specification default of 200 and must be positive.

For each page, create an iteration spec with `page_size`. Omit `marker` on the first request; on continuation requests, pass the previous response marker exactly as returned. Do not pass a filter object and do not send `is_system`, `names`, or `privileges`. Every unset optional field must remain absent rather than becoming null, an empty string, an empty array, false, zero, or an SDK default. Invoke no operation outside the protected contract.

A 401 means the access token expired. Call `RefreshConnection` once for that exact failed request, atomically replace the session's server handle, and retry the identical operation parameters once. Preserve every earlier page. A second 401 for the retry is terminal. Do not refresh for another HTTP status, do not restart pagination, and do not include a token, authentication-header value, or server-handle rendering in an error message. Keep the replacement handle for later inventory calls.

Reject a null page, a missing or null `Items` collection, a null item, an item with a blank `Role`, an item with missing `Info`, an item whose `Info.Name` is blank, a non-string marker, a non-empty marker with an empty page, or a repeated marker. Buffer results until all pages succeed. Return the complete role list sorted by `Info.Name` with `StringComparer.Ordinal`, then by `Role` with `StringComparer.Ordinal`; do not trust server or page order.

Run `pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File .protected/verify.ps1`. The protected verifier generates all tokens, markers, and role data at runtime, starts `mock_vcenter.py` on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port, and reads its fsynced request log. The mock derives its complete allow-list from `docs/contract.json` and serves only `Vcenter.Authorization.Roles_list`. Verification checks the exact GET target and query order, retry-target identity, `vmware-api-session-id` token transition, headers, empty body, marker continuity, complete sorted results, replacement-handle reuse, and omission of every unset optional query field. It never contacts a live VMware endpoint. Everything under `.protected/` and `docs/`, plus the module manifest, is protected; edit only `VcfVcenterRoleInventory/VcfVcenterRoleInventory.psm1`.
scenario: the initial vCenter API session token expires on the second page, so the client refreshes once, retries the same opaque marker, retains the first page, completes pagination, and reuses the refreshed SDK handle on a later full inventory call
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback mock exposes only the named operation and its fsynced request log proves exact marker continuity, retry identity, vmware-api-session-id transition, empty request bodies, and omission of every unset optional field
